walkthroughs.body_html:
Ethical Legal & Environmental Impacts — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ethical Legal & Environmental Impacts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ethical Legal & Environmental Impacts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique involves breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems?
options: Abstraction
Decomposition
Iteration
Encapsulation

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a trace table?
options: To compile code
To track variable values during execution
To draw a flowchart
To store program output

mcqs.q: What does it mean that RAM is volatile?
options: Its contents are lost when power is removed.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
It can explode or be damaged easily.
It can store data permanently.

mcqs.q: What is hexadecimal A in denary?
options: It can store data permanently.
1 (treating A as the first letter).
26 (A's position in the alphabet).

mcqs.q: Why is UDP used for live video streaming despite being unreliable?
options: Lower overhead and latency - retransmitting late packets would harm real-time quality.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
26 (A's position in the alphabet).
Because TCP cannot handle video data.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Algorithm”?
options: Table used to track the changing values of variables as an algorithm executes step by step.
Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.
Diagram using standardised shapes (oval, rectangle, diamond) to represent the flow of an algorithm.
A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.
